description: A second recall match on a different set of memories. One record is the reader's own account of leaving the choir. The other two are near misses: one shares the word choir, and one describes what the reader now does on Thursdays. Recall returns the matching record without padding it with the near misses.

input.cue: Did I ever write down why I left the choir?

tool_evidence.excerpt: I left the choir in March. Rehearsals moved to Thursday nights and I could not keep up with the new pieces.
The choir at my cousin's wedding sang something I did not recognise and it was the best part of the day.
Thursday evenings are for swimming now, and I sleep better on those nights.

criteria: Says briefly why the recalled record answers the question about leaving the choir
Returns the reader's own earlier statement without interpreting what it means about them
Does not propose a connection between the record and anything else
forbidden_claims: Presents the wedding or swimming records as part of why the reader left
Draws a conclusion about the reader's commitment or character
